title: Determine whether Taoyuan open data can support a defensible pedestrian-corridor investigation
summary: Researching candidate revised after a reproducible live-data probe. Row-level retrieval is proven and corridor/infrastructure matching is partially feasible, but accident-event grain, pedestrian-to-location linkage, exposure, sidewalk measurement integrity, mechanism, problem ownership, and domain review remain unresolved.
observed_condition: Taoyuan's 2025 official open-data products expose 94,183 A1/A2 corridor rows with time/location/road/coordinates, 4,226 sidewalk-management rows, an independent annual-count product totaling 94,183, and a separate 88,450-row party product with vehicle, action status and party order. The products are individually usable but do not expose a shared public case identifier across location and party characteristics.
unresolved_core: Determine the true analytical grain of the accident products and whether location, pedestrian-party and infrastructure evidence can be reconciled strongly enough to define a non-causal pedestrian-corridor investigation before any risk ranking or intervention proposal.
time_scope: Primary empirical probe uses ROC 114 / 2025 official products; historical extension remains future work.
disputes_uncertainty: The 94,183 corridor rows contain only 42,329 distinct published row patterns, but the independent annual-count product also totals 94,183; exact repetition is structural and cannot safely be treated as accidental duplication.

The separate party product has 88,450 rows and 41,501 first parties; its party-order tail strongly resembles corridor multiplicity but does not reconcile exactly because products differ in scope/exclusions and expose no shared case identifier.

Strict district + road/section matching to sidewalk context covers about 58.6% of eligible corridor rows; section-stripped matching raises coverage to about 70.2%, and primary-or-intersection matching to about 74.3%, at increased false-match risk.

The sidewalk table mixes aggregate and road-level records, has 59.4% zero road-length values, 62 normalized district-road keys with multiple rows, and suspect measurements including a reported 720 m maximum sidewalk width.

Pedestrian/person involvement exists in the separate party product, including 7,277 person rows and 1,745 walking-action rows, but the published party fields do not locate those parties at corridor coordinates.
No defensible pedestrian or traffic exposure denominator has been established.
No competent local problem owner or transport/domain reviewer has accepted this revised formulation.
diagnosis: The immediate bottleneck is data semantics and cross-product linkage, not intervention design.
A pedestrian-corridor hypothesis remains plausible but unverified because party identity/location and exposure are not jointly observed in the current published products.
Road-name normalization and sidewalk data quality are material measurement problems that could change any shortlist.
prior_attempts: Metadata-only V0.1 candidate proposed corridor discovery from accident, hotspot, sidewalk and roadway datasets.
Live empirical probe retrieved official 2025 corridor, sidewalk, annual-count and party resources and measured their grain, quality and join behavior.
knowledge_frontier: Resolve or bound the relationship among corridor row multiplicity, annual count semantics and party order.
Identify whether a public national/case-level product contains both coordinates and pedestrian/party characteristics with a stable case identifier.
Determine whether an exposure denominator or defensible proxy exists for candidate pedestrian locations.
Validate sidewalk summary rows, units, duplicate road keys and suspect width/length values before association analysis.
Define a conservative spatial/road matching protocol and estimate false-match sensitivity.
Obtain transport/domain review before interpreting recurrence as safety risk.
constraints: Do not call the 94,183 corridor rows 94,183 independent crashes without resolving source grain.
Do not use exact full-row deduplication as an event-count cleaning rule without source-backed justification.
Do not treat section-stripped road-name matching as a verified join; report strict and permissive sensitivity separately.
Do not infer pedestrian risk or causality from recurrence, road-name co-location or sidewalk width alone.
Do not publicly label a corridor dangerous from this probe.
Any road, signal, enforcement or other consequential intervention requires competent authority.
Preserve Government Open Data License Taiwan attribution and source lineage.
authority_boundary: This candidate authorizes public-data retrieval, data-quality analysis, non-causal recurrence analysis and formulation research only. It does not authorize official safety classification, field intervention, road/signal changes, enforcement, procurement or deployment; those remain with competent Taoyuan authorities/operators.
implementation_pathway: Resolve/bound accident analytical grain and cross-product semantics.
Validate sidewalk data and define conservative join rules.
Acquire or derive pedestrian-specific location evidence and exposure information.
Only then generate a non-causal investigation shortlist with uncertainty intervals/sensitivity.
Seek independent transport/domain review and problem-owner correction.
Collect representative field observations for selected candidates if review supports proceeding.
Reframe, verify or retire the packet before any intervention proposal.
rights_notes: The referenced official products state Government Open Data License Taiwan 1.0 where indicated. Raw source datasets are fetched during reproducible probes and are not committed to this repository.

evidence.source: Taoyuan City Police Department open data
evidence.summary: 2025 corridor resource exposes time, area, road/intersection and coordinates. The live probe observed 94,183 rows and structural exact repetition across published fields.
disputes: Published fields do not identify a unique case/event grain.

evidence.source: Taoyuan City Police Department open data
evidence.summary: 2025 party product exposes age, vehicle class, action status, party order and sex; probe observed 88,450 party rows, including 41,501 first parties, 7,277 person-class rows and 1,745 walking-action rows.
disputes: No shared public case identifier/coordinate is exposed for direct linkage to corridor rows; source exclusions differ.

evidence.source: Taoyuan City Department of Public Works open data
evidence.summary: Live probe retrieved 4,226 road-level/aggregate sidewalk rows and found embedded total rows, duplicate normalized district-road keys and suspect field values requiring validation before association analysis.
disputes: Road-level records do not represent intersection geometry or pedestrian exposure.

limitations: No shared public accident ID is exposed in the current products.

success_criteria.baseline: Four official products retrieved but no common case identifier and unresolved corridor multiplicity.
success_criteria.target: A documented source-grain rule and conservative linkage design that a domain/data reviewer accepts as sufficient for non-causal corridor investigation.
success_criteria.measurement: Reconciliation across official product totals/party order plus sampled/manual validation of road/spatial matches and source documentation.
success_criteria.falsification: Source grain cannot be resolved/bounded enough to prevent material count distortion, or linkage error remains too high for corridor interpretation.

success_criteria.baseline: Pedestrian/person rows exist separately from corridor coordinates; exposure absent.
success_criteria.target: Pedestrian-specific location evidence and an exposure denominator/proxy are available with explicit uncertainty and domain-review acceptance.
success_criteria.measurement: Independent review of linkage/exposure design and falsifiable shortlist methodology.
success_criteria.falsification: Pedestrian location cannot be linked/estimated defensibly, exposure cannot be obtained, or review concludes the proposed ranking would be misleading.
guardrails: No public dangerous-road label without authority/evidence

subproblems.title: Resolve or bound accident analytical grain

subproblems.title: Establish pedestrian-specific location and exposure evidence
subproblems.description: Find a case-level source or defensible linkage that identifies pedestrian involvement at locations and obtain/define an exposure denominator or bounded proxy.

subproblems.title: Produce a non-causal investigation shortlist
subproblems.description: Only after semantic/linkage gates pass, identify recurrence candidates with exposure and matching uncertainty explicitly reported.

subproblems.description: Challenge source grain, matching, exposure, shortlist interpretation and any proposed field-observation protocol before public verification.
